messages:
ashley: FYI AcornSearch hit a regression in the /v1/rerank: multi-query batch with per-query candidate lists returns scores that don't line up with the candidates. customer request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d. Repro steps below.

ashley: SAMPLE PAYLOAD
```json
{
  "requests": [
    {"query_id":"q1", "query":"best laptops", "candidates": ["c1","c2","c3"]},
    {"query_id":"q2", "query":"battery life", "candidates": ["c4","c5"]}
  ]
}
```

ashley: EXPECTED (per-query): q1 -> [c1,c2,c3], q2 -> [c4,c5]
ashley: ACTUAL response (flattened mapping seems shifted):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"candidate":"c1", "score":0.8},
    {"candidate":"c2", "score":0.75},
    {"candidate":"c3", "score":0.6},
    {"candidate":"c4", "score":0.6},  // should be 0.9 for q2
    {"candidate":"c5", "score":0.85}
  ]
}
```

ashley: Notes: happens on large batch (they sent 50 queries, each with variable candidate counts). Small batches (<=5) look fine. They used Content-Encoding: gzip and sent ndjson in the request body. Model: reranker-v2.1.

liam: Can you paste full headers and exact body file? also did they use any optional per_query_candidate_counts flag?

ashley: Full headers: Authorization + Content-Encoding: gzip + Content-Type: application/x-ndjson. They did NOT set per_query_candidate_counts. Attaching a raw gz file to the ticket.

morgan: I'll pull logs for rq_0a1b2c3d from rerank-processor cluster. Early suspicion: chunking/flattening step may compute offsets incorrectly when ndjson is gzipped and split across stream boundaries.

liam: Quick guess: we flatten candidate arrays then rely on an offsets list to remap scores. If offsets are off by one (or missing for some queries) you'll see shifts like this. Reproducing locally now with their gz payload.

deploy-bot: Trace started for rq_0a1b2c3d -> https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/rq_0a1b2c3d

morgan: Found a log in rerank-processor-3: "candidate_offset_mismatch: expected 5 but got 4" at 2025-09-14T21:04:12Z. Also a 502 from front-proxy at ~21:04:13Z. Might be a streaming boundary/truncation.

liam: Reproduced with their gz payload. Root cause appears to be our ndjson->flatten parser when a newline falls at a gzip block boundary; we drop an empty candidate array entry during streaming which shifts subsequent offsets. Triggered only when payload compressed and large enough to span multiple gzip members.

liam: Short-term mitigation: if client sets per_query_candidate_counts we can validate lengths and reject the request with 400 before processing. I'll prepare a quick validation patch.

morgan: I'll add infra alerting for candidate_offset_mismatch and a small proxy retry on 502s for large uploads.

ashley: Customer asked for ETA. Can we give an ETA for the validation patch?

liam: I can push a validation PR today (1–2h), roll to canary in staging, and to prod in ~6h pending tests.

sophia: I'll tell AcornSearch: we have a hotfix patch for validation being pushed today; request a short test with gzip disabled as a workaround. They prefer not to re-send uncompressed but will test.

ashley: Workarounds tried: they retried with uncompressed ndjson and the mapping was correct. So disabling gzip is a confirmed workaround.

liam: Long-term: fix streaming parser to handle gzip member boundaries properly + add unit tests for compressed multi-member streams. I'll file an RFC and JIRA.

morgan: Created alert rule and temporary SLO guardrails on large batch sizes until fix lands.

sophia: Customer updated; they appreciate quick triage. Will escalate to premium support for follow-up.

ashley: Keeping thread open until patch is merged and staged. Will update with prod deploy ts.

ashley: UPDATE 2h later: validation PR merged to main and canary deployed to prod-rl1 at 1730000200. Monitoring for candidate_offset_mismatch spikes.

morgan: Observability note: no new spikes post-canary so far.

ashley: Closing ticket with customer after 24h no-regression window. Will reopen if they see any further issues.
